text.p: Lithuanian oil refinery Mazeikiu Nafta said on Friday that its results for the first three months of this year were better than for the same period in 1996 but it still failed to operate profitably.
The company's spokewoman Virginija Kristinaitiene told Reuters that the company's losses amounted to 17.14 million litas for the first three months of 1997 compared to 40.48 million litas last year.
She added that the refinery's turnover rose to 323.62 million litas for the first quarter of this year from 185.52 million litas for the same period in 1996.
"The losses stemmed from a 14 day shut-down in February when the refinery had not crude oil to refine," she said.
The state-run refinery has been plauged by frequent shut-downs and financial problems.
But it hopes for better results this year and its working capital has been boosted by a $40 million Eurobond issue.
Kristinaitiene said that in April the firm hopes to refine 500,000 tonnes of crude, a company record.
She added that the company hoped to make a profit in the second quarter.
